records.source: הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ׀הַ֭לְלוּ עַבְדֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הַֽ֝לְלוּ אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Praise Yah! Praise, servants of YHWH, praise the name of YHWH.
pieces: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! You who serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, give praise; give praise to the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!

L.1: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! Praise, servants of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, praise the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!

R.1: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! You servants of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is!

decisions.reason: The Hebrew is two words: a plural command, "praise!" (hallelu), and Yah, the short form of the divine name (as in 68:5 and Exodus 15:2). It calls the gathered people to praise. Like the full name, Yah is rendered "the LORD", with Yah as the alternative.

Jewish tradition calls Psalms 113-118 the Hallel ("praise") and sings them at the great festivals, Passover above all, with 113-114 before the Passover meal and 115-118 after it. The hymn Jesus and his disciples sang after the Last Supper (Matthew 26:30; Mark 14:26) was probably the second part.

decisions.choice: servants of the LORD: all who worship him
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean the priests and Levites who served in the temple (134:1), but here, as in 135:1 and in verse 2's "now and forever", it most likely means all his worshipers.

decisions.choice: the name of the LORD: the LORD himself, as he has made himself known
decisions.reason: The name stands for the person and what he has shown himself to be (verses 2-3; 8:2).
Readable says what praising his name means (m4).

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} lifts up the lowly

records.source: יְהִ֤י שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֣ה מְבֹרָ֑ךְ מֵֽ֝עַתָּ֗ה וְעַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: May [the] name of YHWH be blessed from now and until forever.
pieces: May the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be blessed from now on and for all time.

L.2: May the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be blessed from now and until forever.

R.2: Let people praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} now and always!

decisions.choice: blessed: praised, spoken of with thanks
decisions.reason: When people "bless" God, they speak well of him with praise and thanks; the word (barukh) is the same one used when God blesses people.
Readable says "praise", the sense of blessing God (m1).

records.gloss: From [the] rising of [the] sun to its setting, to be praised [is] the name of YHWH.
pieces: From where the sun comes up to where it goes down, the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is worthy of praise.

L.3: From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] to be praised.

R.3: Everywhere on earth, from east to west, people should praise the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: from the rising of the sun to its setting: the whole earth
decisions.reason: The phrase most often means from east to west, the whole world (50:1; Malachi 1:11). It could also mean from morning to evening.

decisions.choice: everywhere on earth, from east to west
alternatives: from the rising of the sun to its setting
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likelier sense (m1).

records.gloss: High above all nations [is] YHWH; above the heavens [is] his glory.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is lifted high over every nation; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory rises above the heavens.

L.4: High above all nations [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; above the heavens [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.

R.4: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is far above all the nations. His glory is greater than the sky above.

decisions.reason: The word (ram) is high, lifted up. The LORD is above the nations as their ruler, and his glory is above even the heavens, the highest thing people can see (8:2; 57:6).

records.gloss: Who [is] like YHWH our God, who makes high to sit,
pieces: Who can compare with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, who has taken {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seat on high,

L.5: Who [is] like {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, who sets [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] seat on high,

R.5: There is no one like {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. He sits on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne high above.

decisions.choice: Who is like the LORD: no one
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one" (Exodus 15:11; 35:10). The two descriptions that follow (verses 5-6) set his height against his care for the low.

decisions.choice: makes high to sit: is enthroned on high
decisions.reason: The participle (hammagbihi) with "to sit" pictures the LORD seated as King in the heights.
The question continues into verse 6, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.
Readable gives the answer the question expects (m1).

records.gloss: who makes low to look on the heavens and on the earth?
pieces: who bends low to see what is in the heavens and on the earth?

L.6: who stoops low to look on the heavens and on the earth?

R.6: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} still bends down to see what is happening in the sky and on the earth.

decisions.reason: The participle (hammashpili) is the opposite of "makes high" in verse 5: the God who sits so high bends low to see. Even the heavens are below him.

decisions.choice: the heavens and the earth: all that is below him
alternatives: (enthroned in) the heavens, (looking) on the earth
decisions.reason: The words may go with "look" (he looks down on both), or the two halves of verses 5-6 may pair up: he sits high in the heavens and looks low on the earth.

records.source: מְקִֽימִ֣י מֵעָפָ֣ר דָּ֑ל מֵֽ֝אַשְׁפֹּ֗ת יָרִ֥ים אֶבְיֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: raising from [the] dust [the] poor; from [the] ash heap he lifts [the] needy,
pieces: He lifts the poor up out of the dust and raises those in need from the ash heap,

L.7: He raises from the dust [the] poor; from the ash heap {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lifts [the] needy,

R.7: He lifts poor people out of the dirt. He raises up needy people from the garbage dump.

decisions.reason: Verses 7-8 repeat almost word for word Hannah's song (1 Samuel 2:8), and verse 9 recalls her story: the barren woman given children.

decisions.choice: ash heap: the town's rubbish dump
decisions.reason: The word ('ashpot) is the heap of ashes and refuse outside a town, where outcasts and beggars sat (Job 2:8 has a similar picture).
The sentence continues into verse 8, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.gloss: to make [them] sit with nobles, with [the] nobles of his people.
pieces: to seat them with nobles, beside the leaders of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

L.8: to make [them] sit with nobles, with the nobles of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

R.8: He lets them sit with princes, with the leaders of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

decisions.reason: The word (nadiv) is a noble or prince. Those who sat on the ash heap are given a seat among the highest in the land.

records.gloss: making the barren [woman] of the house dwell [as] a joyful mother of the children. Praise Yah!
pieces: He gives the woman without children a household of her own, a glad mother of children. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

L.9: He settles the barren woman of the house [as] a joyful mother of children. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

R.9: He gives a home and family to the woman who could not have children, and makes her a happy mother. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

decisions.choice: the barren woman: shame turned to joy
decisions.reason: To have no children was a great sorrow and a shame (1 Samuel 1:6-7). Sarah, Rachel and Hannah were all barren before God gave them sons (1 Samuel 2:5).

decisions.choice: settle in the house: give a secure place in a family
alternatives: make her dwell in the house
decisions.reason: The verb (moshivi) is the one used for seating the poor in verse 8. A wife without children was insecure in the household; now she is settled there as a mother.

The Hebrew is two words: a plural command, "praise!" (hallelu), and Yah, the short form of the divine name (as in 68:5 and Exodus 15:2). It calls the gathered people to praise. Like the full name, Yah is rendered "the LORD", with Yah as the alternative.
Readable says what the picture means (m2).
